title: The wider world of the first millennium CE: Africa, Asia, the Andes, and Europe beyond Rome, 1–1000 CE
reviewed: 2026-10-19. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: Mark founds the church of Alexandria
events.summary: Church tradition says Mark, the Gospel writer, brought the faith to Egypt. The Coptic Church counts him as its founder.

source.quote: According to tradition, in AD 49, about 16 years after the Ascension of Jesus, Mark travelled to Alexandria and founded the Church of Alexandria

events.title: Queen Amanitore rules Kush from Meroë
events.summary: Amanitore and her son Natakamani build temples at Naqa and Meroë. Their reign is the best-recorded time of the kingdom.

source.quote: ruling from Meroë in the middle of the 1st century AD

events.title: A Greek sailing guide describes the Red Sea trade
events.summary: The Periplus lists ports from Egypt to India. It names Adulis, Aksum, and Rhapta on the East African coast.

source.quote: a mid-first-century date is now the most commonly accepted

events.title: The Kingdom of Aksum rises
events.summary: Aksum grows into a trading power on the Red Sea. Its ships link Rome and India through the port of Adulis.

source.quote: the kingdom was founded in the 1st century

events.title: Hero of Alexandria builds a steam engine
events.summary: Hero describes the aeolipile, a sphere spun by steam. He also writes on mirrors, pumps, and surveying.

source.quote: found that it best matched the details of an eclipse in 62 AD

events.title: Ptolemy maps the heavens and the Earth
events.summary: Ptolemy's Almagest sets out the Earth-centered sky. His Geography lists the known world with coordinates.

events.title: The Garamantes rule the Sahara from Garama
events.summary: Desert farmers in the Fezzan dig tunnels to tap fossil water. Their capital, Garama, trades with Rome across the sand.

source.quote: The Garamantes first emerged as a major regional power in the mid-2nd century AD

events.title: An African becomes Roman emperor
events.summary: Septimius Severus, born in Leptis Magna, wins the throne. He builds up his home city with a new forum and basilica.

source.quote: was Roman emperor from 193 to 211. He was born in Leptis Magna, Libya, in the Roman province of Africa

events.title: Perpetua and Felicity die in the arena at Carthage
events.summary: A young noblewoman and an enslaved woman are killed for their faith. Perpetua's prison diary survives.

source.quote: c. 182 – c. 203) were Christian martyrs of the third century

events.title: Anthony goes into the Egyptian desert
events.summary: Anthony leaves his village to live alone in the wilderness. His example starts Christian monasticism.

source.quote: among the first known to go into the wilderness (about AD 270)

events.title: Aksum mints its own coins
events.summary: King Endubis strikes gold, silver, and bronze coins. Aksum is the only African state south of Egypt to do so.

source.quote: from the reign of King Endybis around AD 270

events.title: Pachomius founds the first monastery
events.summary: Pachomius gathers monks under one rule and one roof. Communal monasteries spread from here across the Christian world.

source.quote: Pachomius established his first monastery between 318 and 323 at Tabennisi, Egypt

events.title: Augustine of Hippo, bishop and theologian
events.summary: A Numidian convert becomes bishop of Hippo. His Confessions and City of God shape Western Christian thought.

source.quote: 13 November 354 – 28 August 430

events.title: The Nag Hammadi codices are hidden
events.summary: Thirteen papyrus books of Gnostic and other early Christian texts are sealed in a jar. They include the Gospel of Thomas.

source.quote: these codices may have belonged to a nearby Pachomian monastery and were buried after Saint Athanasius condemned the use of non-canonical books in his Festal Letter of 367 A.D.

events.title: The Serapeum of Alexandria is closed
events.summary: The great temple of Serapis is shut as the old religion is banned. It had housed the daughter library of Alexandria.

source.quote: The Serapeum was closed in 392 CE

events.title: Hypatia is killed in Alexandria
events.summary: A mob kills the philosopher and mathematician Hypatia. She had taught astronomy and geometry in the city.

source.quote: born c. 350–370 – March 415 AD

events.title: The Vandals take Carthage
events.summary: Gaiseric's Vandals seize Rome's richest African province. Their fleet then raids across the Mediterranean.

source.quote: In 439 AD, the Vandals renewed their advance eastward and captured Carthage

events.title: The Lydenburg heads are made
events.summary: Iron Age farmers in southern Africa shape seven terracotta heads. They are the oldest known sculptures south of the equator.

source.quote: places these artifacts and the site at around 1410 BP (approximately 500 A.D.)

events.title: Austronesians settle Madagascar
events.summary: Sailors from the Indonesian islands cross the Indian Ocean in outrigger canoes. Their language becomes Malagasy.

source.quote: Madagascar was first permanently settled during or before the mid-first millennium CE (roughly 500 to 700) by Austronesian peoples

events.title: Justinian's army retakes Africa
events.summary: Belisarius lands near Carthage and ends the Vandal kingdom in a year. Africa is Roman again for a century.

source.quote: The Vandalic War (533–534)

events.title: Nubia turns to Christianity
events.summary: The kingdom of Nobatia on the Nile accepts the faith from Egypt. Nubian churches are painted for the next 900 years.

source.quote: In 543, it converted to Coptic Christianity

events.image: File:Great Mosque of Kairouan courtyard and portico.jpg
events.title: Kairouan is founded
events.summary: Arab armies build a garrison town in what is now Tunisia. Its great mosque makes it a center of learning.

source.quote: The city was founded by the Umayyads around 670

events.title: The Kanem Empire forms by Lake Chad
events.summary: A kingdom grows on the caravan routes across the Sahara. It becomes one of the longest-lived states in Africa.

source.quote: The empire is believed to have been founded around the year 700

events.title: Cairo is founded
events.summary: The Fatimids lay out a new capital north of Fustat. It soon holds al-Azhar, one of the oldest universities.

source.quote: Cairo was founded in 969, and became the official seat and capital of the Fatimid Caliphate in 973

events.title: Wang Mang seizes the Han throne
events.summary: A Han official founds the short Xin dynasty. He abolishes slavery and redistributes land, then falls to rebellion.

source.quote: Wang seized the throne in AD 9

events.title: Guangwu restores the Han dynasty
events.summary: Liu Xiu claims the throne and makes Luoyang his capital. By his death the Eastern Han rules all of China.

quote: In the summer of AD 25, after repeated urging by his followers, he finally claimed the title of emperor
consolidated by the time of Emperor Guangwu's death in AD 57

events.title: The Han emperor sends a gold seal to Japan
events.summary: Guangwu gives a gold seal to an envoy from the state of Na. It is Japan's first dated appearance in written history.

source.quote: bestowed by Emperor Guangwu upon a diplomatic envoy visiting from the Yayoi Na state in the year 57 AD

events.title: Buddhism reaches China
events.summary: Emperor Ming founds the White Horse Temple for two monks from India. Tradition calls it China's first Buddhist temple.

source.quote: according to tradition, is the first Buddhist temple in China, having been first established in 68 AD under the patronage of Emperor Ming

events.title: Ban Chao governs the Western Regions
events.summary: The Han general secures the Tarim Basin and the Silk Road. He sends Gan Ying west to find Rome.

source.quote: In 91 CE, Ban Chao finally succeeded in pacifying the Western Regions and was awarded the title of Protector General and stationed at Qiuci (Kucha)

events.title: Zhang Heng presents a seismoscope
events.summary: A bronze vessel drops a ball to show the direction of a distant earthquake. Zhang also maps the stars.

source.quote: In 132, Zhang introduced an intricate seismoscope to the court

events.title: The Yellow Turban Rebellion
events.summary: Peasants led by Daoist healers rise against the Han court. The war that follows breaks the dynasty's power.

source.quote: The uprising broke out in 184 AD

events.image: File:Dai Jin-Looking Three Times at the Thatched Hut.jpg
events.title: The Three Kingdoms divide China
events.summary: Wei, Shu, and Wu fight for the fallen Han empire. Their generals and strategists become China's best-loved legends.

source.quote: The Three Kingdoms of Cao Wei, Shu Han, and Eastern Wu dominated China from 220 to 280 AD

events.title: Queen Himiko sends envoys to Wei
events.summary: A shaman queen of Wa, early Japan, is named in Chinese records. Wei's emperor calls her a friend of Wei.

source.quote: Himiko's emissaries first visited the court of Wei emperor Cao Rui in 238

events.title: The first Mogao Caves are dug at Dunhuang
events.summary: Monks cut cave shrines into a cliff on the Silk Road. Over a thousand years they fill with paintings and scrolls.

source.quote: The first caves were dug out in 366 CE

events.image: File:Guo Xu - Portrait of Xie An (undated).jpg
events.title: The Battle of Fei River
events.summary: A small Eastern Jin army routs the Former Qin invasion. North and south China stay divided for two more centuries.

source.quote: took place in the autumn of 383 AD

events.title: The Gwanggaeto Stele is raised
events.summary: King Jangsu of Goguryeo sets up a stone to honor his father. It is the chief written source for early Korea.

source.quote: erected in 414 by his son Jangsu

events.title: The Yungang Grottoes are carved
events.summary: The Northern Wei court orders giant Buddhas cut into a sandstone cliff. Indian and Chinese styles meet in the carving.

source.quote: starting in the 5th century CE under Imperial auspices

events.title: Work begins on the Longmen Grottoes
events.summary: The Northern Wei move to Luoyang and begin carving Buddhas by the Yi River. Work continues for 600 years.

source.quote: Starting with the Northern Wei dynasty in 493 AD

events.title: Buddhism reaches Japan
events.summary: The king of Baekje sends a Buddha image and sutras to the Japanese court. The Soga clan takes up the new faith.

quote: provides a date of 552 for when King Seong of Baekje (now western South Korea) sent a mission to Emperor Kinmei that included an image of the Buddha Shakyamuni
Other sources, however, give the date of 538

events.title: Xuanzang journeys to India
events.summary: A Chinese monk travels to India for Buddhist texts and studies at Nalanda. He returns with 657 books to translate.

source.quote: the travelogue of his journey to the Indian subcontinent in 629–645

events.title: Alopen brings Christianity to China
events.summary: A Syriac missionary of the Church of the East reaches the Tang court. The Xi'an Stele of 781 records his welcome.

source.quote: the initial Church of the East had met recognition by the Tang Emperor Taizong, due to efforts of the Christian missionary Alopen in 635

events.title: The Taika Reform in Japan
events.summary: After the fall of the Soga clan, the court remakes Japan on the Chinese model. Land and taxes come under the emperor.

source.quote: were a set of doctrines established by Emperor Kōtoku (孝徳天皇 Kōtoku tennō) in the year 645

events.title: Wu Zetian rules China as emperor
events.summary: The only woman to rule China in her own name founds her Zhou dynasty. She favors Buddhism and the examination system.

source.quote: She was the sole ruler of the self-styled Zhou dynasty from 690 to 705

events.title: The An Lushan Rebellion
events.summary: A frontier general marches on the Tang capitals. The eight-year war leaves the dynasty weakened for good.

source.quote: lasted from 755 to 763

events.title: Japan's capital moves to Heian-kyō
events.summary: Emperor Kanmu lays out a grid city on the model of Chang'an. It stays the imperial seat for a thousand years.

source.quote: established by Emperor Kanmu in 794

events.title: Thomas the Apostle reaches India
events.summary: Tradition says the apostle Thomas landed on the Kerala coast. The Saint Thomas Christians trace their church to him.

source.quote: According to tradition, Thomas the Apostle came to Muziris on the Kerala coast in 52 AD

events.title: Roman ships trade for pepper at Muziris
events.summary: Monsoon winds carry Roman ships to the Malabar coast each year. Pepper and gems go west, gold and wine come east.

source.quote: Roman trade links peaked between the 1st century BC and 4th century AD

events.title: Gautamiputra Satakarni revives the Satavahanas
events.summary: The greatest Satavahana king restores his dynasty's power in the Deccan. Its capital is Pratishthana on the Godavari.

source.quote: Charles Higham dates his reign c. 103 – c. 127 CE

events.title: Kanishka rules the Kushan Empire at its height
events.summary: Kanishka rules from Central Asia to the Ganges. He supports Buddhism, and his coins show gods of many faiths.

source.quote: under whose reign (c. 127–150 CE) the empire reached its zenith

events.title: The Rabatak inscription
events.summary: A stone in Bactrian names Kanishka's ancestors and the gods who gave him kingship. It fixed the Kushan family tree.

source.quote: It dates to the 2nd century CE

events.image: File:Hephthalite wearing the crown of Peroz I Late 5th century CE.jpg
events.title: The Hephthalites rule Central Asia
events.summary: The White Huns defeat the Kidarites and press on Persia and India. The Turks and Sasanians bring them down together.

source.quote: militarily important from 450 CE, when they defeated the Kidarites, to 560 CE

events.title: The Huns invade northern India
events.summary: Toramana's Alchon Huns push into central India. The invasions help bring down the Gupta Empire.

source.quote: In the First Hunnic War (496–515), the Alchon reached their maximum territorial extent, with King Toramana pushing deep into Indian territory

events.title: Kashyapa builds his palace on Sigiriya rock
events.summary: A Sri Lankan king makes a fortress on a 180-meter column of granite. Its painted maidens still look out from the cliff.

source.quote: selected by King Kashyapa (CE 477–495) for his new capital

events.title: Aryabhata writes the Aryabhatiya
events.summary: At 23 he sets out arithmetic, algebra, and astronomy in verse. He holds that the Earth turns on its axis.

source.quote: which mentions that in 3600 Kali Yuga, 499 CE, he was 23 years old

events.title: The Mahabodhi Temple is built at Bodh Gaya
events.summary: A brick tower rises where the Buddha is said to have gained enlightenment. It is the holiest Buddhist pilgrimage site.

source.quote: What is now visible on the ground dates from the 6th century CE

events.title: The Chalukyas cut the Badami cave temples
events.summary: Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist shrines are carved into a sandstone cliff at the Chalukya capital.

source.quote: the earliest date from the 6th century

events.title: Harsha rules northern India
events.summary: Harsha unites the north from Kannauj and hosts the pilgrim Xuanzang. His empire breaks up at his death.

source.quote: was the emperor of Kannauj from April 606 until his death in 647

events.title: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram
events.summary: The Pallavas build a granite temple on the beach of their port. It is among the oldest stone temples in south India.

source.quote: The Shore Temple (c. 725 AD)

events.title: The Kailasa temple is carved at Ellora
events.summary: Rashtrakuta masons cut a whole temple downward out of one cliff. It is the largest rock-cut temple in the world.

source.quote: generally attributed to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (r. 756–773 CE)

events.image: File:WLA haa Standing Buddha Pala dynasty.jpg
events.title: The Pala Empire begins in Bengal
events.summary: The chiefs of Gauda elect Gopala as king. His Buddhist dynasty builds great monasteries and trades with Southeast Asia.

source.quote: The empire was founded with the election of Gopāla by the chiefs of Gauda in the late 8th century CE

events.title: Rajaraja I makes the Cholas an empire
events.summary: The Chola king conquers the south and northern Sri Lanka. His navy reaches the Maldives.

source.quote: was a Chola emperor who reigned from 985 to 1014

events.title: The Buddhas of Bamiyan are carved
events.summary: Two giant Buddhas are cut into a cliff on the road between India and China. The Taliban destroyed them in 2001.

events.title: Songtsen Gampo founds the Tibetan Empire
events.summary: The king unites the Tibetan plateau and moves his court to Lhasa. He brings in Buddhism and a script.

source.quote: was the 33rd King (Tsenpo) of Tibet from 618 or 629 until his death in 650, and the founder of the Tibetan Empire

events.title: The Afrasiab murals are painted in Samarkand
events.summary: A Sogdian house is painted with envoys from China, Korea, and Persia. It shows the Silk Road at its busiest.

source.quote: They were probably painted between 648 and 651 CE

events.title: The Samanids rule from Bukhara
events.summary: A Persian dynasty governs Khorasan and Transoxiana. Persian poetry and learning revive at its court.

source.quote: from 819 to 999

events.title: The Trưng sisters rise against Han rule
events.summary: Two sisters lead the Vietnamese against the Chinese governor and rule for three years. They are national heroines.

source.quote: ruled for three years after commanding a rebellion in AD 40 against the first Chinese domination of Vietnam

events.title: Funan, the first kingdom of Southeast Asia
events.summary: A trading state grows in the Mekong Delta. Roman, Indian, and Chinese goods are found at its port, Óc Eo.

source.quote: Funan is believed to have been established in the 1st century CE in the Mekong Delta

events.image: File:Ganesh, My Son E5, 7th century, Quang Nam - Museum of Cham Sculpture - Danang, Vietnam - DSC01715.JPG
events.title: Champa is founded
events.summary: A local official throws off Han rule on the coast of central Vietnam. The Cham kingdoms last until 1832.

source.quote: The state of Champa was founded in AD 192 by Khu Liên (Ou Lian), an official of the Eastern Han dynasty of China in Xianglin who rebelled against Chinese rule in 192

events.title: The Pyu build Sri Ksetra
events.summary: The Pyu wall a city on the Irrawaddy larger than any before Angkor. Buddhist texts are stamped on gold leaves.

source.quote: Sri Ksetra was founded between the fifth and seventh centuries by the Pyu people

events.title: Chenla succeeds Funan
events.summary: Khmer rulers from the interior take over Funan's lands. Their temples at Sambor Prei Kuk come before Angkor.

source.quote: existed from around the late 6th to the early 9th century in Indochina

events.title: The Dvaravati culture of central Thailand
events.summary: Mon towns in the Chao Phraya basin adopt Buddhism and Indian script. Their stone Wheels of the Law survive.

source.quote: dated from about the 6th to the 11th century

events.image: File:Old Bagan, Myanmar, Ancient Buddhist temple in Bagan plains.jpg
events.title: Pagan is walled on the Irrawaddy
events.summary: King Pyinbya fortifies a small town that grows into the first Burmese empire. Thousands of temples later fill its plain.

source.quote: fortified the city in 849 AD

events.title: Prambanan is dedicated in Java
events.summary: A Hindu king consecrates a temple to Shiva near Buddhist Borobudur. It is the largest Hindu temple in Indonesia.

source.quote: the Shiva temple was inaugurated on 12 November 856

events.title: The Laguna Copperplate Inscription
events.summary: A debt is cancelled in writing on a copper plate. It is the oldest known document from the Philippines.

source.quote: inscribed onto a copper plate in the Shaka year 822 (900 A.D.)

events.title: Germanic tribes destroy three Roman legions
events.summary: Arminius ambushes Varus in the Teutoburg Forest. Rome gives up its plans to hold Germany east of the Rhine.

source.quote: between 8 and 11 September 9 AD

events.image: File:Bust of Emperor Claudius - Altes Museum, Berlin (52671298090).jpg
events.title: Rome conquers Britain
events.summary: Claudius sends four legions across the Channel. Within fifty years most of England and Wales is a Roman province.

source.quote: It began in earnest in AD 43 under Emperor Claudius, and was largely completed in the southern half of Britain (most of what is now called England and Wales) by AD 87

events.title: Boudica's revolt
events.summary: The queen of the Iceni burns Colchester, London, and St Albans. Rome crushes the rising within a year.

source.quote: led a failed uprising against the conquering forces of the Roman Empire in AD 60 or 61

events.title: Pliny publishes the Natural History
events.summary: Pliny the Elder's encyclopedia gathers what Romans knew of nature, geography, and art. It mentions the Essenes by the Dead Sea.

source.quote: He published the first 10 books in AD 77

events.title: The Colosseum opens
events.summary: Vespasian begins the amphitheater with spoils from Judea, and Titus opens it. It seats some 50,000 people.

source.quote: Construction began under the Emperor Vespasian (r. 69–79 AD) in 72 and was completed in AD 80

events.title: Hadrian rebuilds the Pantheon
events.summary: A concrete dome 43 meters wide is raised over the temple of all the gods. It is still the largest unreinforced dome.

source.quote: reconstructed under Hadrian (117–138)

events.title: Hadrian's Wall is begun
events.summary: A stone wall with forts runs 117 kilometers across northern Britain. It marks the empire's edge.

source.quote: begun in AD 122 in the reign of the Emperor Hadrian

events.title: Galen comes to Rome
events.summary: The physician from Pergamon becomes doctor to emperors. His books rule Western medicine for 1,400 years.

source.quote: Galen went to Rome in 162 and made his mark as a practicing physician

events.title: The Antonine Plague
events.summary: Soldiers returning from the East bring a deadly epidemic, likely smallpox. It kills millions across the empire.

source.quote: The Antonine Plague of AD 165 to 180

events.title: The Crisis of the Third Century
events.summary: Fifty years of civil war, plague, and invasion nearly break the empire. Diocletian's reforms end the chaos.

source.quote: The period is usually dated between the death of Severus Alexander (235) and accession of Diocletian (284)

events.title: Wulfila translates the Bible into Gothic
events.summary: Wulfila makes an alphabet for the Goths and translates the scriptures. It is the oldest long text in a Germanic language.

source.quote: c. 311 – 383), known also as Wulfila(s) or Urphilas, was a 4th-century Gothic preacher

events.title: The Goths defeat Rome at Adrianople
events.summary: Gothic refugees settled inside the empire destroy the eastern army and kill the emperor Valens.

source.quote: The battle took place on 9 August 378

events.title: Christianity becomes the state religion of Rome
events.summary: Theodosius I orders all subjects to hold the Nicene faith. Other creeds are declared heresies.

source.quote: issued on 27 February AD 380 by Theodosius I, made Nicene Christianity the state church of the Roman Empire

events.title: Jerome begins the Vulgate
events.summary: Pope Damasus asks Jerome to revise the Latin Gospels. Jerome goes on to translate the Old Testament from Hebrew in Bethlehem.

source.quote: who was commissioned by Pope Damasus I in 382 to revise the Vetus Latina Gospels

events.title: The Visigoths sack Rome
events.summary: Alaric's Goths loot the city for three days. Rome had not fallen to an enemy in 800 years.

source.quote: The sack of Rome on 24 August 410 AD was undertaken by the Visigoths led by their king, Alaric

events.title: Patrick preaches in Ireland
events.summary: A Briton once enslaved in Ireland returns as a missionary bishop. His own Confession tells the story.

source.quote: there is general agreement that he was active as a missionary in Ireland during the fifth century

events.title: Attila rules the Huns
events.summary: From the Hungarian plain Attila extorts gold from both Roman empires. He invades Gaul and Italy before his death.

source.quote: was the ruler of the Huns from 434 until his death in early 453

events.title: Clovis unites the Franks
events.summary: A Frankish king conquers most of Gaul and accepts Catholic baptism. His Merovingian line rules for 250 years.

quote: as a king of the Salian Franks in 481

events.title: Justinian codifies Roman law
events.summary: Jurists gather centuries of law into the Code, the Digest, and the Institutes. European civil law descends from it.

source.quote: enacted from 529 to 534 by order of Roman Emperor Justinian I

events.title: The Plague of Justinian
events.summary: Bubonic plague arrives from Egypt and kills a fifth of Constantinople. It returns in waves for two centuries.

source.quote: The plague of Justinian or Justinianic plague (AD 541–549)

events.title: The Lombards invade Italy
events.summary: A Germanic people crosses the Alps and takes most of the peninsula from the Byzantines. Lombardy keeps their name.

source.quote: conquered most of the Italian Peninsula between 568 and 774 AD

events.title: The Sutton Hoo ship burial
events.summary: An East Anglian king is buried in a ship with a helmet, gold, and silver. It was found intact in 1939.

source.quote: It was used in this way from around 575 to 625

events.title: Gregory the Great is pope
events.summary: A former prefect of Rome reforms the Church and feeds the city. He sends missionaries to the English.

source.quote: was the 64th Bishop of Rome from 3 September 590 until his death on 12 March 604

events.title: Augustine's mission reaches Kent
events.summary: Monks sent by Pope Gregory baptize King Æthelberht. Canterbury becomes the seat of the English church.

source.quote: became the first Archbishop of Canterbury in the year 597

events.title: Muslim armies conquer Spain
events.summary: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses from Africa and the Visigothic kingdom falls. Al-Andalus lasts for nearly 800 years.

source.quote: in early 711 to cross the Straits of Gibraltar

events.title: Byzantine iconoclasm begins
events.summary: Emperors ban and destroy religious images. The dispute splits the Church for a century and strains ties with Rome.

source.quote: occurred between about 726 and 787

events.title: Bede finishes his history of the English
events.summary: A monk in Northumbria writes the Ecclesiastical History of the English People. He dates events from the birth of Christ.

source.quote: completed in about 731

events.title: Charles Martel wins at Tours
events.summary: The Franks turn back an Umayyad army from al-Andalus. Charles's grandson will be Charlemagne.

source.quote: was fought on 10 October 732

events.title: The Great Mosque of Córdoba is begun
events.summary: Abd al-Rahman I builds a hall of striped arches on the site of a church. It is now the city's cathedral.

source.quote: The Great Mosque was constructed in 785 on the orders of Abd al-Rahman I

events.title: The Book of Kells is made
events.summary: Monks of Columba's order paint the four Gospels in Latin. Its pages are the finest of Celtic art.

source.quote: It is believed to have been created c. 800 AD

events.title: Norse settlers reach Iceland
events.summary: Farmers from Norway claim an empty island in the North Atlantic. Their descendants write the sagas.

source.quote: generally believed to have begun in the second half of the ninth century

events.title: Cyril and Methodius go to the Slavs
events.summary: Two brothers from Thessalonica devise the first Slavic alphabet. They translate the scriptures and liturgy.

source.quote: In 862, the brothers began the work which would give them their historical importance

events.title: Bulgaria becomes Christian
events.summary: Boris I and his court are baptized by a mission from Constantinople. Bulgaria soon adopts the Slavic liturgy.

source.quote: In the late autumn of 864, a mission from the Patriarch of Constantinople Photios arrived at the Bulgarian capital Pliska and converted the Khan

events.title: Alfred the Great rules Wessex
events.summary: Alfred holds off the Vikings and fortifies his towns. He translates Latin books into English.

source.quote: was King of the West Saxons from 871 to 886, and King of the Anglo-Saxons from 886 until his death in 899

events.title: Oleg takes Kiev
events.summary: A Varangian prince makes Kiev the seat of the Rus'. The state he founds reaches from the Baltic to the Black Sea.

source.quote: Oleg captured Smolensk and later Kiev in 882

events.title: Otto I is crowned emperor
events.summary: The German king is crowned in Rome, reviving the imperial title in the West. It becomes the Holy Roman Empire.

source.quote: Holy Roman Emperor from 962 until his death in 973

events.title: Vladimir baptizes the Rus'
events.summary: The prince of Kiev accepts Orthodox Christianity and marries a Byzantine princess. His people follow him into the Dnieper.

source.quote: Vladimir converted to Christianity in 988, and Christianized the Kievan Rus

events.title: The Mishnah is compiled
events.summary: Judah the Prince gathers the oral law into six orders. It becomes the core of the Talmud.

source.quote: until the compilation of the Mishnah in the late second or early third century CE

events.title: Mani preaches a new religion
events.summary: A prophet from Babylonia presents his faith to Shapur I. Manichaeism spreads from Africa to China.

source.quote: Returning in 242, Mani presented himself to Shapur I

events.title: The painted synagogue of Dura-Europos
events.summary: A synagogue on the Euphrates is painted with scenes from the Hebrew Bible. A Roman rampart preserved the walls.

source.quote: The last phase of construction was dated by an Aramaic inscription to 244 CE

events.title: Shapur I captures a Roman emperor
events.summary: The Sasanian king defeats Valerian and takes him prisoner. Rock reliefs in Persia show the emperor kneeling.

source.quote: in Edessa (now the Turkish city of Urfa) in 260

events.title: Zenobia of Palmyra seizes the Roman East
events.summary: The queen of a desert trading city takes Egypt and Syria. Aurelian defeats her and leads her through Rome in chains.

source.quote: In 270, Zenobia launched an invasion that brought most of the Roman East under her sway

events.title: Armenia adopts Christianity
events.summary: King Tiridates III is converted by Gregory the Illuminator. Armenia is the first state to make Christianity official.

source.quote: In the early 4th century (301, according to tradition) Tiridates adopted Christianity as the state religion of Armenia

events.title: The Great Persecution of Christians
events.summary: Diocletian orders churches razed and scriptures burned. It is Rome's last and harshest persecution.

source.quote: The Diocletianic Persecution (303–312), the empire's last, largest, and bloodiest official persecution of Christianity

events.title: Constantine builds the Church of the Holy Sepulchre
events.summary: A church rises over the sites held to be Golgotha and the tomb of Jesus. Pilgrims have come ever since.

quote: About 326, Constantine ordered that the temple to Jupiter or Venus be replaced by a church
The church was consecrated on 13 September 335

events.title: The Codex Sinaiticus is written
events.summary: Scribes copy the whole Greek Bible onto parchment. It is the oldest complete New Testament.

source.quote: is a fourth-century Christian manuscript of a Greek Bible

events.title: The Council of Ephesus
events.summary: Bishops condemn Nestorius and name Mary Theotokos, the bearer of God. The Church of the East goes its own way.

source.quote: convened in Ephesus (near present-day Selçuk in Turkey) in AD 431

events.title: The Council of Chalcedon
events.summary: Over 500 bishops define Christ as one person in two natures. The churches of Egypt, Syria, and Armenia reject it.

source.quote: from 8 October to 1 November 451

events.title: The Babylonian Talmud is completed
events.summary: The academies of Sura and Pumbedita finish their commentary on the Mishnah. It becomes the central text of Judaism.

source.quote: The text was most likely completed, however, in the 6th century

events.title: Saint Catherine's Monastery is built at Sinai
events.summary: Justinian walls a monastery around the traditional burning bush. It is the oldest monastery still in use.

source.quote: it was built between 548 and 565

events.image: File:Capital of Khosrow II, Taq-e Bostan.jpg
events.title: The Persians take Jerusalem
events.summary: Khosrow II's army captures the city during the long war with Byzantium. Heraclius later wins it back.

source.quote: The Sasanian conquest of Jerusalem in early 614

events.title: The Battle of the Yarmuk
events.summary: Arab armies destroy the Byzantine field army in six days. Syria and Palestine pass to the caliphate.

source.quote: lasted for six days in August 636

events.title: The Sasanian Empire falls at Nahavand
events.summary: The last Persian army is broken. Yazdegerd III flees east and the caliphate takes Iran.

source.quote: was fought in 642 between the Rashidun Muslim forces

events.image: File:The Umayyad Mosque, the Courtyard, Damascus, Syria.jpg
events.title: The Umayyad Caliphate rules from Damascus
events.summary: Mu'awiya makes the caliphate hereditary. In ninety years it reaches from Spain to the Indus.

source.quote: ruled by the Umayyad dynasty from 661 to 750

events.title: Husayn is killed at Karbala
events.summary: The grandson of Muhammad dies with his small band against the Umayyad army. Shia Muslims mourn the day each year.

source.quote: was fought on 10 October 680

events.title: The Abbasids take the caliphate
events.summary: A revolt from Khurasan overthrows the Umayyads. The new dynasty soon builds Baghdad and rules for 500 years.

source.quote: The Abbasids rose to power in 750, when the Abbasid Revolution overthrew the preceding Umayyad Caliphate

events.title: Al-Khwarizmi writes on algebra
events.summary: A scholar at the House of Wisdom sets out methods for solving equations. The words algebra and algorithm come from his work.

source.quote: Around 820, he worked at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad

events.title: The Great Mosque of Samarra
events.summary: The caliph al-Mutawakkil builds the largest mosque in the world. Its spiral minaret still stands.

source.quote: The mosque was commissioned in 848 CE and completed in 851

events.title: The Aleppo Codex is written in Tiberias
events.summary: Masoretic scribes finish the most accurate copy of the Hebrew Bible. Maimonides later endorsed it.

source.quote: The codex was written in the city of Tiberias in the tenth century CE (circa 920)

events.title: Cahuachi, ceremonial center of the Nazca
events.summary: Forty adobe mounds rise above the Nazca Lines. Pilgrims gather here from across the valley.

source.quote: based from about 1–500 CE

events.title: The stone figures of San Agustín
events.summary: Hundreds of carved guardians watch over tombs in the Colombian highlands. It is the largest necropolis in the Americas.

source.quote: they are believed to have been carved between 5–400 AD

events.title: Pachacamac is founded
events.summary: A shrine to the creator god grows on the coast south of Lima. Pilgrims come to its oracle for 1,300 years.

source.quote: The site was first settled around A.D. 200

events.title: The Quimbaya goldsmiths
events.summary: Craftsmen in the Cauca valley cast gold and copper figures and flasks. Their work is the finest in ancient Colombia.

source.quote: The Quimbaya people reached their zenith during the 4th to 7th century CE period known as The Quimbaya Classic

events.title: The painted tombs of Tierradentro
events.summary: Underground chambers reached by spiral stairs are painted in red, black, and white. They hold the bones of the dead.

source.quote: the park features hypogea dating from 6th to 9th centuries AD

events.image: File:Jar, Huari Empire, Peru, 600-900 AD, ceramic - Fowler Museum - University of California, Los Angeles - DSC02374.jpg
events.title: The Wari Empire
events.summary: From Ayacucho the Wari rule much of Peru with roads and provincial centers. The Inca later follow their model.

source.quote: emerged in around 600 CE in Peru's Ayacucho Basin

events.title: The Marajoara culture of the Amazon
events.summary: People at the mouth of the Amazon build mounds and paint elaborate pottery. They farm the floodplain.

source.quote: the culture appeared to flourish between 800 AD and 1400 AD
